cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: GELU Activation (Exact)
description: Computes the Gaussian Error Linear Unit x·Φ(x), the activation used in BERT, GPT and most transformers.
notes: Smooth and slightly negative for small negative inputs, unlike ReLU.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: GELU Activation (tanh Approximation)
description: Computes the fast tanh approximation of GELU used in the original GPT-2 code.
notes: Differs from the exact GELU by less than 0.0005 everywhere.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: ELU Activation
description: Computes the exponential linear unit: x for positive inputs, α(eˣ − 1) otherwise (Clevert et al. 2015).
notes: Pushes mean activations towards zero, which can speed up learning.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: SELU Activation
description: Computes the scaled exponential linear unit, whose constants make activations self-normalise to zero mean and unit variance (Klambauer et al. 2017).
notes: Pair it with LeCun-normal initialisation and alpha-dropout.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Mish Activation
description: Computes Mish, x·tanh(softplus(x)), a smooth self-gated activation used in YOLOv4.
notes: Similar in shape to Swish/SiLU.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Hard Sigmoid
description: Computes the piecewise-linear sigmoid used on mobile networks: x/6 + 0.5 clipped to [0, 1] (PyTorch convention).
notes: Cheaper than the exponential in the true sigmoid.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Hard Swish
description: Computes the hard-swish activation of MobileNetV3: x·ReLU6(x + 3)/6.
notes: A cheap approximation of Swish.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: ReLU6 Activation
description: Clips ReLU at 6, which keeps activations in a range that low-precision arithmetic can represent (MobileNet).
notes: min(max(0, x), 6).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Softsign Activation
description: Computes x/(1 + |x|), a tanh-like activation that approaches its limits polynomially rather than exponentially.
notes: Saturates more gently than tanh.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Tanh Derivative
description: Gives the slope of tanh at x, used in back-propagation.
notes: At most 1 (at x = 0), so deep tanh networks still suffer from vanishing gradients.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Softmax of a Logit Vector
description: Turns a list of logits into probabilities that add up to 1; the largest logit is subtracted first for numerical stability.
notes: The result is a list with one probability per class.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Softmax with Temperature (Vector)
expression: exp(z / tmp - max(z / tmp)) / sum(exp(z / tmp - max(z / tmp)))
description: Divides the logits by a temperature before the softmax: T < 1 sharpens the distribution, T > 1 flattens it.
notes: Used for sampling from language models and for knowledge distillation.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Log-Sum-Exp
description: Computes ln Σ e^zᵢ stably by factoring out the maximum; a smooth approximation of max(z).
notes: The normaliser of the softmax and the core of cross-entropy.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Log-Softmax of One Class
description: Gives the log-probability of class k from the logits: z_k − logsumexp(z).
notes: Always compute this form rather than ln(softmax) to avoid underflow.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Multiclass Cross-Entropy from Logits
description: Gives the categorical cross-entropy loss for one example from its logits and true class.
notes: Equal to −ln p_k; divide by ln 2 for bits.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Label-Smoothed Cross-Entropy
expression: (1 - eps) * (max(z) + ln(sum(exp(z - max(z)))) - at(z, k)) + eps * (max(z) + ln(sum(exp(z - max(z)))) - mean(z))
description: Mixes the one-hot target with a uniform distribution before computing cross-entropy, which discourages over-confident predictions (Szegedy et al. 2016).
notes: ε = 0.1 is the common choice for image classification and translation.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Softmax Cross-Entropy Gradient w.r.t. Logits
expression: exp(z - max(z)) / sum(exp(z - max(z))) - (seq(1, len(z), 1) == k)
description: Gives the gradient of the softmax cross-entropy loss with respect to each logit: softmax(z) minus the one-hot target.
notes: This simple form is why softmax and cross-entropy are always paired.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Focal Loss

variables.label: Predicted probability of the true class

description: Down-weights easy, well-classified examples so training focuses on hard ones (Lin et al. 2017, RetinaNet).
notes: γ = 0 gives weighted cross-entropy; γ = 2 is standard for dense object detection.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Soft Dice Loss
description: Gives 1 − Dice coefficient on soft predictions, the standard loss for medical image segmentation where the object is small.
notes: The smoothing term avoids division by zero on empty masks.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Contrastive Loss (Pair)
description: Pulls matching pairs together and pushes non-matching pairs at least a margin apart (Hadsell, Chopra and LeCun 2006).
notes: Used for Siamese networks in face verification and signature checking.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Triplet Loss
description: Asks the anchor to be closer to a positive example than to a negative one by at least a margin (FaceNet, Schroff et al. 2015).
notes: Mining hard triplets matters more than the exact loss.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Cosine Similarity of Two Vectors
description: Gives the cosine of the angle between two vectors of any length; 1 means the same direction.
notes: The standard similarity for text and image embeddings.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Dense Layer Parameter Count
description: Counts the weights and biases of a fully connected layer.
notes: A 768 → 3072 layer (the first half of a BERT-base feed-forward block) has 2,362,368 parameters.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: MLP Parameter Count from Layer Sizes
expression: sum(k, 1, len(l) - 1, at(l, k) * at(l, k + 1) + at(l, k + 1))
description: Adds the weights and biases of every layer of a fully connected network.
notes: The classic 784-256-128-10 MNIST network has 235,146 parameters.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Conv2D Parameter Count
description: Counts the parameters of a 2-D convolution with a k × k kernel.
notes: Independent of the image size, which is why convolutions are parameter-efficient.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Depthwise-Separable Convolution Parameters
expression: k^2 * cin + cin + cin * cout + cout
description: Counts the parameters of a depthwise k × k convolution followed by a 1 × 1 pointwise convolution (MobileNet, Xception).
notes: About 1/cout + 1/k² of a standard convolution: 8,960 here against 73,856.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Convolution Output Size
description: Gives the spatial size of a convolution or pooling output: ⌊(W − K + 2P)/S⌋ + 1.
notes: The ResNet stem turns 224 × 224 into 112 × 112.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Transposed Convolution Output Size
description: Gives the output size of a transposed ("de-")convolution used for up-sampling in decoders and GANs.
notes: Kernel 4, stride 2, padding 1 exactly doubles the size.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Dilated Convolution Effective Kernel Size
description: Gives the span covered by a kernel with gaps of d − 1 between its taps (atrous convolution, WaveNet, DeepLab).
notes: Widens the receptive field without adding parameters.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Receptive Field of Stacked Convolutions
expression: 1 + sum(i, 1, len(ks), (at(ks, i) - 1) * prod(j, 1, i - 1, at(st, j)))
description: Gives the size of the input region that influences one output unit of a stack of convolution or pooling layers.
notes: Each layer adds (k − 1) times the product of all earlier strides.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Convolution Multiply–Accumulate Count
description: Counts the multiply–accumulate operations of one convolution layer; double it for FLOPs.
notes: Used to estimate inference cost on phones and edge devices.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: LSTM Layer Parameter Count
description: Counts the parameters of one LSTM layer: four gates, each with input weights, recurrent weights and a bias.
notes: Frameworks with two bias vectors per gate (e.g. cuDNN) add another 4h.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: GRU Layer Parameter Count
description: Counts the parameters of one GRU layer with three gates.
notes: About three quarters of an LSTM of the same size.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Embedding Table Parameters
description: Counts the entries of a token embedding table.
notes: GPT-2 small spends 38.6 million of its 124 million parameters here.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Xavier (Glorot) Uniform Initialisation Limit
description: Gives the bound a of the uniform distribution U(−a, a) that keeps activation variance stable through tanh/sigmoid layers (Glorot and Bengio 2010).
notes: The normal version uses standard deviation √(2/(fan_in + fan_out)).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: He (Kaiming) Normal Initialisation Std
description: Gives the standard deviation that keeps activation variance constant through ReLU layers (He et al. 2015).
notes: The factor 2 compensates for ReLU zeroing half of its inputs.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: LeCun Normal Initialisation Std
description: Gives the standard deviation 1/√fan_in recommended for SELU networks and for the output of linear layers.
notes: Also the default scale in many transformer implementations.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Batch Normalisation Output
description: Normalises an activation with the batch statistics and applies the learned scale and shift (Ioffe and Szegedy 2015).
notes: At inference time the running mean and variance replace the batch values.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Layer Normalisation of a Vector
description: Normalises a vector of activations to zero mean and unit variance across its features (Ba et al. 2016), before the learned scale and shift.
notes: Used in every transformer block; unlike batch norm it does not depend on the batch.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: RMSNorm of a Vector
description: Scales a vector by the reciprocal of its root mean square, without subtracting the mean (Zhang and Sennrich 2019).
notes: Cheaper than layer norm; used in LLaMA, Mistral and most recent LLMs.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Inverted Dropout Scale
description: Gives the factor by which kept activations are multiplied during training, so no rescaling is needed at inference.
notes: With p = 0.1 kept units are scaled by about 1.111.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Single Neuron Output (Sigmoid)
description: Computes a neuron's output: the sigmoid of the weighted sum of its inputs plus a bias (logistic regression is the same unit).
notes: Swap the sigmoid for another activation as needed.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Perceptron Weight Update
description: Applies Rosenblatt's perceptron rule (1958): weights move towards the input when the prediction is wrong.
notes: Converges if the classes are linearly separable.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: L1 (Lasso) Penalty
description: Adds λΣ|wᵢ| to the loss, which drives many weights exactly to zero (sparsity).
notes: Combine with the L2 penalty for the elastic net.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Elastic Net Penalty
description: Mixes L1 and L2 penalties (Zou and Hastie 2005): sparse like the lasso, stable with correlated features like ridge.
notes: α = 1 is pure lasso, α = 0 pure ridge (scikit-learn convention).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Vanishing Gradient Bound for Sigmoid Layers
description: Gives the largest possible product of sigmoid derivatives across n layers (each at most 1/4), showing why deep sigmoid networks stop learning.
notes: Ten layers can shrink the gradient by a factor of about a million; ReLU and residual connections avoid this.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Linear Warm-up Learning Rate
description: Ramps the learning rate linearly from 0 to its peak over the warm-up steps, which stabilises the start of transformer training.
notes: Usually followed by a decay schedule.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Warm-up then Cosine Decay Learning Rate
expression: if(t < w, lr * t / w, lmin + 0.5 * (lr - lmin) * (1 + cos(pi * (t - w) / (tt - w))))
description: The standard LLM schedule: linear warm-up, then cosine decay to a floor at the last step.
notes: GPT-3 and LLaMA decay to about 10 % of the peak.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Inverse Square-Root (Noam) Learning Rate
description: The schedule of the original Transformer paper (Vaswani et al. 2017): linear warm-up, then decay proportional to 1/√step.
notes: Peaks at step w with value (d·w)^(−1/2).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Step Decay Learning Rate
description: Multiplies the learning rate by γ every s epochs, the classic ImageNet ResNet schedule.
notes: With γ = 0.1 and s = 30 the rate is 0.001 in epoch 65.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Polynomial Decay Learning Rate
description: Decays the learning rate as a polynomial of the remaining fraction of training; power 1 is linear decay (BERT).
notes: Power 0.9 is common in segmentation ("poly" schedule).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Cyclical (Triangular) Learning Rate
expression: lo + (hi - lo) * max(0, 1 - abs(t / hs - 2 * floor(1 + t / (2 * hs)) + 1))
description: Moves the learning rate back and forth between two bounds in a triangle wave (Smith 2017).
notes: Also the basis of the learning-rate range test.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Warm-up–Stable–Decay (WSD) Learning Rate
expression: piecewise(t < w, lr * t / w, t < td, lr, lr * (1 - (t - td) / (tt - td)) + lmin * (t - td) / (tt - td))
description: Warm up, hold the rate constant, then decay quickly at the end (MiniCPM 2024), which lets training be extended without restarting the schedule.
notes: The short final decay often gives most of the loss improvement.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: SGD with Momentum: Velocity Update
description: Updates the velocity of momentum SGD; the parameter then moves by the new velocity.
notes: Momentum 0.9 averages gradients over roughly the last 10 steps.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Effective Learning Rate with Momentum
description: Gives the step size that momentum SGD effectively takes on a steady gradient: lr/(1 − μ).
notes: Momentum 0.9 multiplies the effective step by 10.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Adam First-Moment Update
description: Updates Adam's exponential moving average of gradients.
notes: Bias-correct it by dividing by 1 − β₁ᵗ.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Adam Second-Moment Update
description: Updates Adam's exponential moving average of squared gradients.
notes: LLM training often lowers β₂ to 0.95 for stability.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Adam Parameter Step
description: Gives how far Adam moves a parameter: learning rate × bias-corrected m / (√bias-corrected v + ε) (Kingma and Ba 2014). Subtract it from the parameter.
notes: At step 1 the step is about lr × sign(g), independent of the gradient scale.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: AdamW Decoupled Weight Decay Update
description: Applies AdamW: the adaptive Adam step plus weight decay applied directly to the weights, not through the gradient (Loshchilov and Hutter 2019).
notes: Weight decay 0.1 is typical for LLM pre-training.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: RMSprop Update Step
expression: lr * g / (sqrt(rho * v + (1 - rho) * g^2) + eps)
description: Gives the RMSprop step: the gradient divided by the root of a running mean of squared gradients (Hinton's 2012 lecture).
notes: Subtract from the parameter.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Adagrad Update Step
description: Gives the Adagrad step, which shrinks the learning rate for parameters that have seen large gradients (Duchi et al. 2011).
notes: Good for sparse features; the rate keeps shrinking, which RMSprop and Adam fix.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Gradient Clipping by Global Norm
description: Rescales a gradient whose norm exceeds the threshold so its norm equals the threshold, leaving its direction unchanged.
notes: A max norm of 1.0 is standard in LLM training to stop loss spikes.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Exponential Moving Average of Weights
description: Keeps a slowly moving average of the weights, which often generalises better than the latest weights (Polyak averaging, used in diffusion models).
notes: A decay of 0.999 averages over about the last 1000 steps.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Effective Batch Size
description: Gives the number of examples per optimiser step with gradient accumulation and data parallelism.
notes: Multiply by the sequence length for tokens per step.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Linear Learning-Rate Scaling Rule
description: Scales the learning rate in proportion to the batch size (Goyal et al. 2017, training ImageNet in one hour).
notes: Needs warm-up at large batches; Adam-type optimisers often use square-root scaling instead.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Square-Root Learning-Rate Scaling Rule
description: Scales the learning rate with the square root of the batch-size ratio, which keeps the noise scale of adaptive optimisers roughly constant.
notes: Commonly used with Adam and LAMB.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Training Steps per Epoch
description: Gives the optimiser steps needed to see every example once.
notes: ImageNet-1k with batch 256 takes 5005 steps per epoch.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Tokens Seen in Training
description: Multiplies steps, batch size and sequence length to give the total training tokens.
notes: 250k steps × 1024 × 4096 ≈ 1.05 trillion tokens.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Balanced Class Weight
description: Weights a class by the inverse of its frequency so every class contributes equally to the loss (scikit-learn "balanced").
notes: A class with 5 % of the data gets weight 6.67 among three classes.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Effective Number of Samples (Class-Balanced Loss)
description: Estimates how many distinct examples a class effectively has, because extra samples of a class overlap (Cui et al. 2019); weight classes by its inverse.
notes: β → 1 recovers inverse-frequency weighting.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Knowledge Distillation Loss (Soft Targets)
expression: tmp^2 * sum(exp(zt / tmp - max(zt / tmp)) / sum(exp(zt / tmp - max(zt / tmp))) * (ln(exp(zt / tmp - max(zt / tmp)) / sum(exp(zt / tmp - max(zt / tmp)))) - ln(exp(zs / tmp - max(zs / tmp)) / sum(exp(zs / tmp - max(zs / tmp))))))
description: Gives T² × KL(teacher ‖ student) between temperature-softened output distributions (Hinton, Vinyals and Dean 2015).
notes: Usually mixed with the ordinary cross-entropy on the true labels.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Cross-Validation Standard Error
description: Gives the standard error of the mean score across k cross-validation folds.
notes: Folds share training data, so this understates the true uncertainty somewhat.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Grid Search Size

variables.label: Number of values for each hyperparameter

description: Counts the training runs a full grid search needs: the product of the number of values per hyperparameter.
notes: Grows exponentially with the number of hyperparameters; random search scales better.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Random Search: Chance of a Top-q Configuration
description: Gives the probability that at least one of n random configurations lands in the best fraction q of the search space (Bergstra and Bengio 2012).
notes: 60 trials give a 95 % chance of hitting the top 5 %.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Gradient Descent Convergence Rate on a Quadratic
description: Gives the per-step error reduction factor of gradient descent with the best fixed step on a quadratic with condition number κ.
notes: Ill-conditioned problems (large κ) converge slowly; momentum improves the rate to (√κ − 1)/(√κ + 1).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Optimal Step Size for a Quadratic
description: Gives the fixed learning rate that minimises the worst-case convergence factor of gradient descent: 2/(L + μ).
notes: Rates above 2/L make gradient descent diverge.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Newton Step in One Dimension
description: Moves to the minimum of the local quadratic model: x − f'(x)/f''(x).
notes: Converges quadratically near a minimum, but needs second derivatives.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Bias–Variance Decomposition of Expected Error
description: Splits a model's expected squared error into bias², variance and irreducible noise.
notes: Simple models have high bias; flexible ones high variance.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Early-Stopping Patience Trigger
expression: sum(k, len(vl) - pt + 1, len(vl), at(vl, k) >= at(cummin(vl), len(vl) - pt) - md) == pt
description: Returns 1 when none of the last "patience" epochs improved on the best validation loss by at least the minimum delta, the usual early-stopping rule.
notes: Here the best loss 0.6 came three epochs ago, so training stops.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Gradient Accumulation Steps
description: Gives how many micro-batches each GPU must accumulate before an optimiser step to reach a target global batch size.
notes: Accumulation trades time for memory: same maths, fewer GPUs.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Critical Batch Size (Gradient Noise Scale)

variables.label: Trace of the per-example gradient covariance tr(Σ)
Squared norm of the true gradient |G|²

description: Estimates the batch size beyond which larger batches give diminishing speed-ups — the "simple noise scale" (McCandlish et al. 2018).
notes: It grows as training loss falls, so batch size can grow during training.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Transformer Non-Embedding Parameters (12·L·d²)
description: Approximates the parameters in a standard transformer's attention and MLP blocks (4d² + 8d² per layer), the N used in scaling laws (Kaplan et al. 2020).
notes: GPT-3 (96 layers, d = 12288) gives about 174 billion; embeddings add the rest of its 175 billion.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Llama-Style Decoder Parameter Count
expression: nl * (d * d + 2 * d * kv * (d / nh) + d * d + 3 * d * ff + 2 * d) + d + 2 * vocab * d
description: Counts the parameters of a LLaMA-style model: attention with grouped key/value heads, a SwiGLU MLP (three matrices), RMSNorm weights, and untied input and output embeddings.
notes: LLaMA-2 7B comes out at exactly 6,738,415,616.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Training Compute (6ND)
description: Estimates the floating-point operations to train a dense transformer: about 6 per parameter per token (2 forward, 4 backward).
notes: Chinchilla (70B params, 1.4T tokens) used about 5.9 × 10²³ FLOPs.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Inference Compute per Generated Token
description: Estimates the FLOPs to produce one token: 2 per parameter plus the attention over the context (Kaplan et al. 2020).
notes: The attention term matters only for long contexts.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Chinchilla Compute-Optimal Tokens
description: Gives the roughly compute-optimal number of training tokens for a model size: about 20 tokens per parameter (Hoffmann et al. 2022).
notes: Models meant for cheap inference are now trained far beyond this (e.g. LLaMA-3 8B on 15T tokens).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Chinchilla Compute-Optimal Model Size
description: Solves C = 6·N·(20N) for N: the model size that uses a compute budget optimally under the 20-tokens-per-parameter rule.
notes: 5.76 × 10²³ FLOPs gives about 69 billion parameters (Chinchilla).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Chinchilla Scaling-Law Loss L(N, D)
description: Predicts pre-training loss from model size and data with the fitted law E + A/N^α + B/D^β (Hoffmann et al. 2022).
notes: E = 1.69 is the irreducible loss of the text; the constants apply to that paper's data and tokenizer only.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Kaplan Scaling Law: Loss vs Parameters
description: Predicts the loss of a model trained to convergence on enough data as (N_c/N)^0.076 (Kaplan et al. 2020).
notes: Doubling the model lowers the loss by about 5 %.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Kaplan Scaling Law: Loss vs Data
description: Predicts the loss of a large model trained with early stopping on D tokens as (D_c/D)^0.095 (Kaplan et al. 2020).
notes: Constants depend on the tokenizer and data set.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Effective Data with Repeated Epochs
description: Estimates how many fresh tokens repeated data is worth: repeats lose value exponentially (Muennighoff et al. 2023, R* ≈ 15.4).
notes: Up to about 4 epochs repetition is nearly as good as new data.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Training Time from Compute
description: Converts a compute budget into wall-clock days for a given cluster and utilisation.
notes: The default is H100 dense BF16 peak (989 TFLOP/s) at 40 % MFU.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Model FLOPs Utilisation (MFU)
description: Compares the useful model FLOPs actually achieved (6N per token) with the hardware peak (Chowdhery et al. 2022, PaLM).
notes: 40–55 % is good for large dense-model training.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: GPU-Hours for a Training Run
description: Gives the total accelerator time needed, independent of how many GPUs share it.
notes: Multiply by the hourly price for a cost estimate.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Training Energy

variables.label: Power per GPU incl. server share

description: Estimates the electricity used by a training run from GPU-hours, power draw and the data centre's power usage effectiveness.
notes: Multiply by the grid's carbon intensity (kg CO₂/kWh) for emissions.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Model Weight Memory
description: Gives the memory needed just to hold the weights: 16-bit weights take 2 bytes per parameter, 4-bit ones half a byte.
notes: A 70B model needs 140 GB in BF16 and about 35 GB in 4-bit.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Training Memory with Adam (Mixed Precision)
description: Estimates weights, gradients and Adam state at 16 bytes per parameter (2 + 2 + 12), divided across GPUs with full sharding (Rajbhandari et al. 2020, ZeRO).
notes: Activations come on top and depend on batch and sequence length.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: KV Cache Memory
expression: 2 * nl * kv * hd * ctx * bsz * bpe / 1e9
description: Gives the memory for cached keys and values during generation: 2 × layers × KV heads × head size × tokens × batch × bytes.
notes: LLaMA-3 70B (80 layers, 8 KV heads) needs about 2.7 GB for one 8k-token sequence; grouped-query attention cut this eightfold.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Attention Matrix Memory (Naive)
description: Gives the memory to store the full n × n attention matrix of one layer, which grows with the square of the context.
notes: FlashAttention avoids materialising it, which is what made long contexts practical.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Decode Speed Limit from Memory Bandwidth
description: At batch size 1 every weight must be read once per token, so tokens per second cannot exceed bandwidth divided by model size.
notes: A 7B model in BF16 (14 GB) on an H100 (3.35 TB/s) tops out near 240 tokens/s; batching raises total throughput.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Roofline Attainable Performance
description: Gives the performance a kernel can reach: limited by compute or by memory bandwidth × arithmetic intensity, whichever is lower (Williams et al. 2009).
notes: Below the ridge point (peak/bandwidth ≈ 295 FLOP/byte here) a kernel is memory-bound.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Arithmetic Intensity of a Matrix Multiply
expression: 2 * m * n * k / (bpe * (m * k + k * n + m * n))
description: Divides the 2mnk FLOPs of an m×k by k×n matrix product by the bytes moved to read the inputs and write the output.
notes: Large square products are compute-bound; batch-1 decoding (m = 1) is memory-bound.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Prefill Latency Estimate
description: Estimates the time to process a prompt before the first output token (compute-bound): 2N FLOPs per prompt token.
notes: Time to first token grows with prompt length.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: End-to-End Generation Latency
description: Adds the time to first token and the time to generate the remaining output at the decode speed.
notes: For long answers the decode speed dominates.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Perplexity from Cross-Entropy Loss
description: Converts a language model's average cross-entropy (in nats) to perplexity, the effective number of equally likely next tokens.
notes: A loss of 2.1 nats is a perplexity of about 8.2.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Bits per Byte
description: Converts per-token loss into bits per byte of raw text, which compares models with different tokenizers fairly.
notes: Lower is better; it measures how well the model compresses text.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention Weights
expression: exp(mmul(kk, q) / sqrt(len(q)) - max(mmul(kk, q) / sqrt(len(q)))) / sum(exp(mmul(kk, q) / sqrt(len(q)) - max(mmul(kk, q) / sqrt(len(q)))))
description: Computes softmax(K·q/√d): how much one query attends to each key (Vaswani et al. 2017).
notes: Dividing by √d keeps the dot products from growing with the head size.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Attention Output Vector
expression: mmul(trans(vv), exp(mmul(kk, q) / sqrt(len(q)) - max(mmul(kk, q) / sqrt(len(q)))) / sum(exp(mmul(kk, q) / sqrt(len(q)) - max(mmul(kk, q) / sqrt(len(q))))))
description: Mixes the value vectors with the attention weights: Σ softmax(K·q/√d)ᵢ · vᵢ.
notes: The weights come from the keys; the content comes from the values.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Self-Attention FLOPs per Layer
description: Counts the multiply-adds of the two attention matrix products (QKᵀ and attention × V) for one layer and one sequence, forward pass.
notes: Quadratic in the sequence length, unlike the linear projections.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Sinusoidal Positional Encoding Value
description: Gives dimension i of the original transformer's fixed positional encoding: sine for even i, cosine for odd i, with wavelengths from 2π to 10000·2π.
notes: Relative positions become linear functions of these vectors.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: RoPE Rotation Angle
description: Gives the angle by which rotary position embedding rotates pair i of a query or key at a position (Su et al. 2021).
notes: Low pairs rotate fast (local positions), high pairs slowly (long range). LLaMA-3 uses base 500,000.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: RoPE Longest Wavelength
description: Gives the wavelength of the slowest-rotating RoPE pair, roughly the longest distance the encoding can tell apart.
notes: Raising the base stretches this for longer contexts.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: NTK-Aware RoPE Base Scaling
description: Raises the RoPE base so a model can read contexts s times longer with little fine-tuning (NTK-aware scaling, 2023).
notes: A 4× extension raises base 10,000 to about 40,900.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: ALiBi Head Slope
description: Gives the slope of the linear distance penalty added to attention scores in head h (ALiBi, Press et al. 2022).
notes: Heads get geometrically spaced slopes 1/2, 1/4, … 1/256 for eight heads.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Nucleus (Top-p) Set Size
expression: sum(k, 1, len(pr), sum(j, 1, k - 1, at(sort(pr), len(pr) + 1 - j)) < tp)
description: Counts the most likely tokens needed for their probabilities to reach p; nucleus sampling draws only from these (Holtzman et al. 2020).
notes: The set adapts: small when the model is confident, large when it is not.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Repetition Penalty on a Logit

variables.label: Logit of a token already generated

description: Makes already-generated tokens less likely by dividing positive logits (or multiplying negative ones) by θ (Keskar et al. 2019, CTRL).
notes: θ = 1 means no penalty; 1.1–1.3 is common.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Entropy of a Next-Token Distribution
description: Measures how uncertain the model is about the next token; exp(entropy) is the effective number of choices.
notes: Used to detect hallucination-prone steps and to adapt sampling.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: LoRA Trainable Parameters
description: Counts the parameters of low-rank adapters: each adapted d_in × d_out matrix gets A (r × d_in) and B (d_out × r) (Hu et al. 2021).
notes: Rank 16 on the four attention matrices of 32 layers is about 16.8 million parameters, 0.25 % of a 7B model.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Symmetric INT8 Quantisation Scale
description: Gives the scale that maps [−max|x|, max|x|] onto the int8 range [−127, 127].
notes: Outliers inflate the scale and waste precision, which per-channel and group-wise schemes address.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Quantise a Value (Symmetric)

variables.label: Largest integer (127 for int8, 7 for int4)

description: Maps a real value to its integer code: round(x/scale) clipped to the representable range.
notes: Dequantise by multiplying the code by the scale.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Asymmetric Quantisation Zero Point
description: Gives the uint8 code that represents 0 when [min, max] is mapped onto 0 … 255 with scale (max − min)/255.
notes: Suits activations such as ReLU outputs that are not centred on zero.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Speculative Decoding Expected Tokens per Step
description: Gives the expected number of tokens produced per verification step when a draft model proposes γ tokens, each accepted with probability α (Leviathan et al. 2023).
notes: With α = 0.8 and γ = 4, about 3.4 tokens per target-model pass.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Speculative Decoding Speed-up

variables.label: Draft cost relative to the target model

description: Estimates the wall-clock speed-up of speculative decoding: expected tokens per step divided by the cost of γ draft passes plus one target pass.
notes: A draft model 20× cheaper gives about 2.8× here.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Mixture-of-Experts Total and Active Parameters
description: Gives the parameters actually used per token in a mixture-of-experts model: shared weights plus k experts in each MoE layer.
notes: Mixtral 8×7B has about 47B parameters in total but only about 13B active per token.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Switch Transformer Load-Balancing Loss

variables.label: Fraction of tokens routed to each expert

description: Adds α·E·Σ fᵢ Pᵢ to the loss so the router spreads tokens evenly over experts (Fedus et al. 2021).
notes: Equals α when routing is perfectly uniform.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Tokens from Text Length
description: Estimates the token count of a text from its length and the tokenizer's average characters per token.
notes: English averages about 4 characters (0.75 words) per token with GPT-style tokenizers; Japanese is closer to 1–1.5.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: LLM API Cost
description: Gives the cost of a workload priced per million input and output tokens.
notes: Output tokens usually cost several times more than input tokens; cached input is often discounted.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: KL-Penalised Reward (RLHF)
description: Gives the reward used in RLHF: the reward-model score minus β times the log-ratio to the reference model, which keeps the policy from drifting (Ouyang et al. 2022).
notes: β trades reward against staying close to the supervised model.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: DPO Loss (One Preference Pair)

variables.label: Policy log-prob of the preferred answer
Reference log-prob of the preferred answer
Policy log-prob of the rejected answer
Reference log-prob of the rejected answer

description: Computes the direct preference optimisation loss −ln σ(β·[(log πw − log πref,w) − (log πl − log πref,l)]) (Rafailov et al. 2023).
notes: Trains on preference pairs directly, without a separate reward model or RL loop.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Bradley–Terry Preference Probability
description: Gives the probability that answer A is preferred to B from their scalar rewards (Bradley and Terry 1952); reward models for RLHF are trained on this.
notes: A reward gap of 1 means about 73 % preference.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: GRPO Group-Relative Advantage

variables.label: Rewards of all answers in the group

description: Scores an answer against the other answers sampled for the same prompt: (r − group mean)/group std (DeepSeekMath 2024, used for DeepSeek-R1).
notes: Removes the need for a separate value network.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Discounted Return
description: Adds future rewards discounted by γ per step: G = Σ γᵏ rₖ, the quantity an RL agent maximises.
notes: γ close to 1 values the far future; 0.99 is common.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Effective Planning Horizon
description: Gives the rough number of steps a discount factor looks ahead: 1/(1 − γ).
notes: γ = 0.99 cares about roughly the next 100 steps.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Temporal-Difference Error
description: Computes δ = r + γV(s') − V(s), the surprise that drives TD learning and actor–critic methods.
notes: Positive means things went better than expected.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: TD(0) Value Update
description: Moves the value estimate a fraction α of the way toward the TD target r + γV(s') (Sutton 1988).
notes: The basis of most value-based RL.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Q-Learning Update
description: Updates an action value toward r + γ max Q(s', ·), learning the optimal policy while following another (Watkins 1989).
notes: Deep Q-networks use the same target with a neural network.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: SARSA Update

variables.label: Q(s', a') of the action actually taken next

description: Updates toward the value of the action the agent actually takes next (on-policy), which makes it more cautious than Q-learning near risky states.
notes: Named after the tuple (s, a, r, s', a').

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Epsilon-Greedy Decay
description: Decays the exploration rate geometrically to a floor: the agent explores less as it learns.
notes: After 2000 steps at 0.999 per step, ε ≈ 0.135.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: UCB1 Action Score
description: Scores a bandit arm by its mean reward plus an exploration bonus that shrinks as the arm is tried more (Auer et al. 2002).
notes: Pick the arm with the highest score; regret grows only logarithmically.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Thompson Sampling Posterior Mean (Beta–Bernoulli)
description: Gives the mean of the Beta posterior for an arm's success rate; Thompson sampling draws from this posterior to choose arms.
notes: Also the Laplace-smoothed conversion rate used in A/B testing.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: PPO Clipped Objective (One Sample)
expression: min(rt * adv, clamp(rt, 1 - ep, 1 + ep) * adv)
description: Gives PPO's clipped surrogate objective for one sample, which stops the policy from changing too much in one update (Schulman et al. 2017).
notes: Here the ratio 1.35 is clipped to 1.2, so the objective is 2.4.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Generalised Advantage Estimate (GAE)
description: Computes the advantage as a (γλ)-weighted sum of future TD errors (Schulman et al. 2016), trading bias against variance with λ.
notes: λ = 0.95 and γ = 0.99 are the usual PPO settings.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Policy Entropy (Discrete Actions)
description: Measures how random the policy is; an entropy bonus in the loss keeps agents exploring.
notes: Maximum ln(number of actions) for a uniform policy.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Soft Target Network Update (Polyak)
description: Moves the target network slowly toward the online network, stabilising DDPG, TD3 and SAC.
notes: τ = 0.005 is standard.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Diffusion Noise Schedule ᾱ_t (Linear β)
description: Gives ᾱ_t = Π(1 − β_s), the share of the original signal variance left after t noising steps with the linear schedule of DDPM (Ho et al. 2020).
notes: At the last step almost no signal is left (ᾱ ≈ 4 × 10⁻⁵).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Cosine Noise Schedule ᾱ(t)
description: Gives the cosine schedule of Nichol and Dhariwal (2021), which destroys information more gradually than the linear one.
notes: Improves image quality with fewer steps.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Diffusion Signal-to-Noise Ratio
description: Gives the signal-to-noise ratio ᾱ/(1 − ᾱ) at a diffusion step; many loss weightings and samplers are expressed in terms of it.
notes: Often plotted as log-SNR.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Noised Sample x_t (Forward Diffusion)
description: Jumps straight to step t of the forward diffusion: x_t = √ᾱ x₀ + √(1 − ᾱ) ε.
notes: The network is trained to predict ε (or x₀, or v) from x_t.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Predicted Clean Sample from Predicted Noise
description: Recovers the model's estimate of the clean sample from its noise prediction, the key step of DDIM sampling.
notes: Inverts the forward-diffusion formula.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Classifier-Free Guidance
description: Pushes the conditional prediction away from the unconditional one to follow the prompt more closely (Ho and Salimans 2022).
notes: Stable Diffusion defaults to a scale of 7.5; higher values trade diversity for prompt adherence.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: VAE KL Divergence Term (Diagonal Gaussian)
description: Computes KL(q(z|x) ‖ N(0, I)) for a diagonal Gaussian encoder, the regulariser of the variational autoencoder (Kingma and Welling 2014).
notes: Weight it by β for a β-VAE.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Reparameterisation Trick Sample
description: Draws z = μ + σε with ε ~ N(0, 1), which lets gradients flow through the sampling step of a VAE.
notes: σ = exp(log-variance/2).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: GAN Discriminator Loss
description: Gives the discriminator's binary cross-entropy for one real and one generated sample (Goodfellow et al. 2014).
notes: At the equilibrium D = 0.5 everywhere, the loss is 2 ln 2.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: GAN Generator Loss (Non-Saturating)
description: Gives the non-saturating generator loss −ln D(G(z)), which gives strong gradients early in training when the discriminator easily wins.
notes: Replaces the original minimax form ln(1 − D).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Latent Diffusion Compression Factor
description: Gives how many times fewer numbers the diffusion model works on in latent space than in pixel space.
notes: Stable Diffusion's 8× VAE with 4 channels compresses 48-fold.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Vision Transformer Patch Count
description: Gives the number of image tokens a Vision Transformer makes by cutting the image into p × p patches (Dosovitskiy et al. 2021).
notes: ViT-B/16 on 224 × 224 images uses 196 patches plus a class token.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Intersection over Union of Two Boxes
expression: max(0, min(ax2, bx2) - max(ax1, bx1)) * max(0, min(ay2, by2) - max(ay1, by1)) / ((ax2 - ax1) * (ay2 - ay1) + (bx2 - bx1) * (by2 - by1) - max(0, min(ax2, bx2) - max(ax1, bx1)) * max(0, min(ay2, by2) - max(ay1, by1)))
description: Gives the overlap of two axis-aligned bounding boxes divided by their union, the standard match score in object detection.
notes: A detection usually counts as correct at IoU ≥ 0.5.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Dice from IoU
description: Converts an IoU (Jaccard) score into the equivalent Dice (F1) score.
notes: Dice is always at least as large as IoU.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Mean Intersection over Union (mIoU)
description: Averages the per-class IoU in semantic segmentation, the standard benchmark metric (PASCAL VOC, Cityscapes).
notes: Rare classes count as much as common ones.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Pixel Accuracy
description: Gives the share of pixels labelled correctly in a segmentation map.
notes: Can look high when a background class dominates; prefer mIoU.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Generalised IoU (GIoU)

variables.label: Area of the smallest enclosing box

description: Extends IoU so non-overlapping boxes still get a useful gradient: subtract the empty share of the enclosing box (Rezatofighi et al. 2019).
notes: Ranges from −1 to 1; loss = 1 − GIoU.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Distance IoU (DIoU)
description: Penalises IoU by the squared centre distance relative to the enclosing box diagonal, speeding up box regression (Zheng et al. 2020).
notes: Used in YOLO-family losses and DIoU-NMS.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Box Centre and Size to Corners
description: Converts a (centre, width) box format to a corner coordinate, as when switching between YOLO and Pascal VOC formats.
notes: Use the same formula with y and height for the vertical corners.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Anchor Box Count per Image
description: Counts the candidate boxes a multi-scale detector scores: grid cells at every stride times anchors per cell.
notes: YOLOv5 at 640 px scores 25,200 boxes before NMS.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Feature Pyramid Level for an RoI
description: Assigns a region of interest to the pyramid level matching its size, P₂ small to P₅ large (Lin et al. 2017, FPN).
notes: Clamp the result to the levels the network has.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Pooling Output Size
description: Gives the spatial size after a max- or average-pooling layer.
notes: ResNet's 3 × 3 stride-2 max pool halves 112 to 56.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Image Tensor Memory
description: Gives the memory of a batch of images stored as N × C × H × W values.
notes: A batch of 32 RGB 224 px images in FP32 is about 19 MB.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Pixel Normalisation (ImageNet)
description: Scales a pixel to 0–1 and standardises it with the dataset channel statistics; ImageNet uses means (0.485, 0.456, 0.406) and stds (0.229, 0.224, 0.225).
notes: Use the same statistics the model was trained with.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Fréchet Distance between Gaussians (1-D FID)
description: Gives the squared Fréchet (2-Wasserstein) distance between two normal distributions, the one-dimensional case of the FID score for generative models (Heusel et al. 2017).
notes: Real FID uses 2048-dimensional Inception features and matrix square roots.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Inception Score from Class Entropies

variables.label: Entropy of the marginal class distribution

description: Gives the Inception Score exp(E[KL(p(y|x) ‖ p(y))]) = exp(H(y) − E[H(y|x)]): high when images are confidently classified and classes are diverse (Salimans et al. 2016).
notes: Upper bound is the number of classes (1000).

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Optical Flow Endpoint Error
description: Gives the Euclidean error of an optical-flow vector; averaged over pixels it is the EPE reported on Sintel and KITTI.
notes: KITTI also reports the share of pixels with error above 3 px.

cat: Deep learning and large language models
name: Object Keypoint Similarity (One Keypoint)
description: Scores a predicted pose keypoint like IoU does for boxes, allowing for object size and how precisely that joint can be labelled (COCO keypoints).
notes: κ is 0.026 for the nose and 0.107 for hips.
